lessons.claim: In optical-tweezer 3-point bending, the beam formula κ_center = 48EI/L³ is the **rigidly clamped** value. If both ends are finite-stiffness traps the chain translates bodily and the static stiffness the driving trap feels drops to 0.682x (at n=25 and κ_end/k_t=0.463, 4830.7 → 3294.2 kT/d²). The chain-bend spec wrote 48EI/L³ as 'the value the driving trap feels' and was 32% wrong. ★ The cause is that it starred κ_end/k_t ~ 1 as 'inside the measurement window' itself and yet derived the boundary condition as rigid -- deliberately putting the stiffness ratio near 1 guarantees that the boundary-condition assumption breaks.
